cards.title: Comparisons
cards.body: `>`, `<`, `>=` and `<=` compare two values and give `true` or `false`.

hi.title: Comparisons
hi.body: `>`, `<`, `>=` aur `<=` do values compare karte hain aur `true` ya `false` dete hain.

cards.title: if, else if, else
cards.body: `if` runs the code in its braces only when the condition is true. `else if` tries another condition, and `else` catches the rest. Only the first match runs.

hi.title: if, else if, else
hi.body: `if` apne braces ka code tabhi chalata hai jab condition true ho. `else if` ek aur condition try karta hai, aur `else` baaki sab pakad leta hai. Sirf pehla match chalta hai.

cards.title: Spot the bug
cards.body: JavaScript stops with a `SyntaxError` before running anything. Which line is wrong?

bug.fix: `else` takes no condition: it catches everything left. Write `} else {`, or `} else if (temp > 0) {`.

hi.title: Bug dhoondo
hi.body: JavaScript kuch bhi chalane se pehle `SyntaxError` dekar ruk jaata hai. Kaunsi line galat hai?
hi.fix: `else` koi condition nahi leta: woh baaki sab pakad leta hai. `} else {` likho, ya `} else if (temp > 0) {`.

check.question: What does this print?
check.explanation: `x > 0` is false, so JavaScript tries `x === 0`, which is true.

hi.question: Yeh kya print karega?
hi.explanation: `x > 0` false hai, isliye JavaScript `x === 0` try karta hai, jo true hai.

exercise.prompt: Read a whole number. Print `positive` if it is greater than 0, `negative` if it is less than 0, and `zero` otherwise.
exercise.promptHi: Ek whole number padho. Agar woh 0 se bada hai toh `positive`, 0 se chhota hai toh `negative`, warna `zero` print karo.
